text: The emperor gives a thumbs down.
Except... nobody knows that.
Gladiators: the thumbs down myth.
Roman writers say the crowd turned their thumbs.
Turned which way? They never said.
It might have been up. Or sideways.
Some think a hidden thumb meant mercy.
So where did thumbs down come from?
A painting. 1872.
A French artist painted the crowd, thumbs down.
It was a huge hit.
Then the movies borrowed it.
Also, most fights didn't end in death.
Gladiators were expensive to train.
Losing one was like wrecking a sports car.
Many walked out alive, to fight again.
Some even became celebrities.
Which way the thumb went: unknown.
Roman sources saying "thumbs down": zero.
Anyway, here's the emperor. Thumbs down.
